source.title: Selective regularization for alignment-focused representation engineering

record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments on organizing color embeddings with selective regularization, but does not test feature superposition, capacity competition, polysemanticity, SAE features, or the dimensionality of superposed features.
record.gate_note: The 2-layer MLP autoencoder maps 3D RGB inputs to a 4D bottleneck, so the experiment does not test storing more sparse features than dimensions. It imposes structure through training regularization rather than measuring whether features spontaneously overlap under capacity pressure. The post also discusses sparse labels and concept anchoring, which are not sparse feature activations in the claim's sense.
record.test_reason: The post trains a tiny color autoencoder (3D RGB input, 4D bottleneck) with imposed regularization and concept anchoring. It has no overcomplete sparse features, no polysemanticity analysis, no SAE or LLM, and no test of feature dimensionality, so its results bear on no version of the superposition claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that selective, weakly supervised regularization and anchoring produced partially structured, predictable color latent spaces, and that anchoring one concept influenced nearby representations. They say scaling to language models remains an open question.
record.recipe_differences: This is a color-autoencoder experiment using training-time selective regularization, not a test or reproduction of the Toy Models of Superposition method. It uses a 4D bottleneck for 3D RGB inputs and does not study sparse overcomplete features.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports that full-color-space training from the beginning performed better and was more consistent across random initializations than curriculum-based training.

fits_no_version.finding: Selective regularization plus a single red anchor yielded a color-wheel arrangement, with other hues spaced regularly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time concept anchoring with weak stochastic labels can organize unanchored concepts around the anchor in a small autoencoder.

fits_no_version.finding: Full-color-space training with selective regularization was reported as better and more consistent than curriculum training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this setup, non-curriculum selective regularization gives more consistent latent structure across random seeds.

record.problems: The evidence is from a simple color domain and a tiny MLP autoencoder; the post itself notes that transfer to language models is unverified. It reports no quantitative results or uncertainty estimates for the described outcomes and does not establish a control comparison for the superposition claim.

untested.parts: All of it: no setting with more sparse features than dimensions, no sparsity transition, no superposition geometry.
All of it: no capacity competition or neuron polysemanticity measured.
All of it: polysemanticity is not measured.
All of it: no LLMs and no dictionary or SAE recovery.
All of it: no SAE features evaluated.
All of it: the dimensionality of features is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The record's assessment is accurate. The post is about representation engineering, not superposition. It reports no quantitative results or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Whether overcomplete sparse features are stored as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, and whether sparsity produces transitions or regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.
No LLM representations or sparse features recovered with a dictionary or SAE are studied.
No SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status is evaluated.
The post does not test whether the features represented by a network are 1D directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP autoencoder
rows.operation_detail: Trained with planarity, unitarity, angular repulsion, and selective concept-anchoring regularization.

conditions.value: selective regularization; vibrant hues stochastically regularized to the first-two-dimension plane

rows.measure: Organization of color embeddings in latent space
rows.value: The post reports that similar colors clustered predictably and vibrant hues formed a clear circle in the first two dimensions, resembling a color wheel.
rows.note: This is a reported color-embedding result, not evidence about sparse-feature superposition.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. The structure is induced by planarity, unitarity and anchoring regularization. It is not superposition.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP autoencoder
rows.operation_detail: Applied stochastic concept anchoring to red during training, with planar constraints.

conditions.value: pure red labeled red approximately 50% of the time; other colors received the label with decreasing probability
no colors other than red anchored to a point

rows.measure: Effect of anchoring red on the organization of other colors
rows.value: The post reports that other primary and secondary colors took positions spaced around the circle at regular intervals.
rows.locator: Key findings — Effectiveness of minimal concept anchoring
rows.note: The result concerns explicitly regularized color concepts, not naturally arising overlap of sparse features.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. This is the effect of the training-time anchor on other colors, with no capacity pressure.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP autoencoder
rows.operation_detail: Compared curriculum learning with training on the full color space from the beginning using selective regularization.

conditions.value: full color space from the beginning versus curriculum-based training

rows.measure: Quality and consistency of resulting structure
rows.value: Training on the full color space from the beginning produced superior results and was more consistent across different random initializations.
rows.locator: Key findings — Selective vs. curriculum-based regularization
rows.note: The post gives no numerical comparison.
rows.check: This compares the study's own training regimens (method choice), so it should be flagged as a method comparison rather than a main result. It has no numbers.
